title: Adjuvant ribociclib + endocrine therapy

agents.name: Ribociclib
agents.explanation: Ribociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6, proteins that help cells move through the cycle of division. Endocrine therapy reduces the hormone signal that can drive HR-positive breast cancer.
agents.watch: Keep blood and ECG appointments. Fever, jaundice, fainting, palpitations, severe rash or new breathlessness need prompt advice.
risks: Rare serious lung or skin reactions

agents.name: Aromatase inhibitor ± ovarian suppression
agents.alias: Letrozole or anastrozole; ovarian suppression when indicated
agents.explanation: The aromatase inhibitor reduces oestrogen production. Before menopause, ovarian suppression is also required; men receiving this AI combination need the appropriate LHRH-agonist plan under product information. The endocrine treatment is taken on a separate schedule and normally continues after ribociclib.
agents.watch: Discuss joint symptoms, hot flushes, sexual symptoms and bone health. Keep ovarian-suppression appointments if prescribed.
risks: Injection-site symptoms if ovarian suppression is prescribed

context_label: Adjuvant · HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer
purpose: For eligible higher-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer, ribociclib is added to endocrine therapy to reduce recurrence risk.
schedule_summary: The usual adjuvant starting dose is ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to three years. The aromatase inhibitor continues every day on its own plan; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.

phases_title: Each phase in your treatment plan
phases_note: The order depends on the indication and your recovery. The whole-treatment map shows how local treatment and ongoing medicines relate to each other.
medicines_title: Your medicines and their different roles
timeline_note: Planned treatment days are distinct from broad possible symptom patterns. Symptoms can occur outside these bands.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Fever, shivers, sudden illness, new breathing problems or severe symptoms need prompt advice on any day, including a treatment break.
teachback: Which medicine is taken when, which test is due next, who reviews it, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, benefit and uncertainty, important medicine-specific risks, reproductive precautions, symptom support and planned duration. Confirm the endocrine partner and any ovarian-suppression plan. The timeline does not authorise a restart or certify clinical review.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, jaundice, marked bleeding, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, chest symptoms or a severe rash promptly.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: NCCP classifies ribociclib as oral moderate–high emetic risk. Agree preventive or rescue treatment under local policy after QT and CYP3A interaction review; no default QT-prolonging antiemetic is selected by this information card.

support.title: Heart rhythm and electrolytes
support.text: Attend the baseline and cycle 1 Day-14 ECG and scheduled electrolyte checks. Fainting, palpitations or severe dizziness need urgent assessment.

support.title: Blood and liver monitoring
support.text: Keep two-weekly blood tests during cycles 1–2 and pre-cycle tests during cycles 3–6. Report fever, jaundice, dark urine or new breathing/skin symptoms promptly.

support.title: AI and ovarian-suppression support
support.text: The aromatase inhibitor continues during the ribociclib rest week and generally after ribociclib completion. Discuss menopause, joints, sexual health, bone risk and any injection-site symptoms from ovarian suppression.

support.title: Completion and follow-up
support.text: Ribociclib has a planned maximum three-year course. Confirm the endocrine duration and early-breast surveillance plan separately; new symptoms should be assessed without waiting for a routine appointment.

questions.a: The usual adjuvant starting dose is ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to three years. The aromatase inhibitor continues every day on its own plan; ovarian suppression is added when indicated. At completion of the planned three-year ribociclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

questions.q: Which checks happen before and during treatment?
questions.a: FBC, renal and liver profile; potassium, calcium, magnesium and phosphorus. ECG before initiation; QTcF must be below 450 ms. Correct electrolytes and review QT/CYP3A interactions. Confirm stage, recurrence-risk criteria, prior treatment, AI and ovarian-suppression plan; reconcile the NCCP node-negative eligibility/exclusion conflict before selection. FBC, renal and liver profile every two weeks for cycles 1–2, then before cycles 3–6, then as clinically indicated. Electrolytes before each of the first six cycles, then as clinically indicated. Repeat ECG around cycle 1 Day 14, then as clinically indicated. Increase liver monitoring for grade 2 or worse abnormalities; review fever, jaundice, palpitations/fainting, breathlessness and severe skin symptoms. Keep early-breast surveillance and bone/endocrine follow-up distinct from treatment-toxicity checks and from metastatic response imaging.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing without personal information. Your hospital arranges actual appointments; ask who books each test and who reviews its result.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Take ribociclib once daily with or without food; swallow whole. Avoid grapefruit. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Confirm any clinical hold and restart with the team. The endocrine partner follows a separate prescription. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: What does the evidence mean for me?
questions.a: Ribociclib added to an aromatase inhibitor reduced the chance of invasive cancer returning in the study. Recent longer follow-up also reported a favorable survival finding, but that analysis was descriptive and needs that qualification. Your treatment team can explain how the study matches your recurrence risk.

questions.q: What happens after treatment changes or ends?
questions.a: At completion of the planned three-year ribociclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan. Keep the separately agreed disease follow-up, endocrine and bone-health plan.

evidence.population: 5,101 adults with HR-positive/HER2-negative stage II–III early breast cancer, including selected high-risk node-negative disease.
evidence.interpretation: Ribociclib added to an aromatase inhibitor reduced the chance of invasive cancer returning in the study. Recent longer follow-up also reported a favorable survival finding, but that analysis was descriptive and needs that qualification. Your treatment team can explain how the study matches your recurrence risk.
evidence.limitations: Your team can discuss the strength and limitations of the evidence alongside treatment risks and alternatives.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: For eligible higher-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer, ribociclib is added to endocrine therapy to reduce recurrence risk.

items.title: Who this treatment is for
items.text: HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer at high recurrence risk: stage IIA with qualifying nodal/high-risk factors, or stage IIB–III, as specified by NCCP. Current NCCP00892v2 includes selected node-negative eligibility and a conflicting node-negative exclusion; clinical reconciliation remains required.

items.title: Schedule and duration
items.text: The usual adjuvant starting dose is ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to three years. The aromatase inhibitor continues every day on its own plan; ovarian suppression is added when indicated. At completion of the planned three-year ribociclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

chapters.title: What the studies tell us
chapters.intro: Ribociclib added to an aromatase inhibitor reduced the chance of invasive cancer returning in the study. Recent longer follow-up also reported a favorable survival finding, but that analysis was descriptive and needs that qualification. Your treatment team can explain how the study matches your recurrence risk.

items.title: How to interpret this
items.text: Study results describe groups with defined treatment and eligibility. Ask about your own likely benefits, important harms, alternatives and remaining uncertainty.

chapters.intro: At completion of the planned three-year ribociclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

items.title: Continue, hold or stop
items.text: The team confirms the plan for each medicine and the next review. Do not restart a clinically held treatment from this educational timeline.

phases.label: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy
phases.detail: Each 28-day cycle has 21 days taking ribociclib and 7 days off. A clinical review confirms each restart.

phases.label: Endocrine therapy continues
phases.detail: Stopping ribociclib does not automatically stop the endocrine medicine or ovarian suppression. Bone-health and symptom review continue.

day_groups.title: Your reference cycle
day_groups.body: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.
day_groups.action: Check the agreed prescription and contact the team for new symptoms. Restart only after the team confirms the plan.

chronology_notes.text: Can occur at any time; broad bands are not measured risk curves.

chronology_notes.title: Checks and restart
chronology_notes.text: Keep the arranged blood / heart appointments. A calendar day alone does not authorise the next dose.

chronology_notes.title: Day 25–26
chronology_notes.text: An optional local pre-cycle review window, not a universal NCCP requirement. Early two-weekly tests and the Cycle 1 Day 14 ECG remain necessary.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the exact medicine, strength, endocrine partner, baseline tests and first review appointments. Ask who arranges tests and who reviews the results.

sections.title: Taking treatment
sections.text: Take ribociclib once daily with or without food; swallow whole. Avoid grapefruit. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Confirm any clinical hold and restart with the team. The endocrine partner follows a separate prescription.

sections.title: Treatment duration
sections.text: At completion of the planned three-year ribociclib course, continue the separately agreed endocrine and follow-up plan.

sections.title: Supply and appointments
sections.text: Request the next supply before tablets run out. Blood tests and any ECG or injections need their own appointments. This oral treatment does not itself require a central line or infusion pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask which medicine is held, whether the endocrine partner continues, what needs to recover, when the next review is due and who will authorise restart.

sections.title: Support between appointments
sections.text: Keep the oncology contact details and prescribed symptom medicines accessible. New severe symptoms need prompt assessment rather than waiting for the next blood test.
